A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. # OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable first-person forest exploration game in the currently empty PlayGround repo, with no interactive objects, detailed procedural forest, PC/mobile controls, and a compatibility warning offering Potato Mode.

## Requirements
- First-person exploring game with no objects (testing build).
- Detailed forest map.
- PC controls: WASD to move, SPACE to jump.
- Mobile controls: left-bottom joystick to move, right-bottom jump button.
- Warning at very start saying exactly: “This game is likely not compatible for Lower devices to handle High graphics, do you want to turn on Potato Mode? You can Turn it on at the Settings on the right top of your screen or Press ESC if you're on PC.”
- Prompt buttons exactly “Turn On” and “Maybe Later”.
- Important warning text highlighted.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them.

## Decisions
- Built as a static Three.js site (`index.html` + ES modules), no build step, vendored Three.js r170.
- Interpreted “no objects” as no collectibles/quests/interactables; environment detail is allowed.
- Warning shown immediately over start screen; ESC on warning enables Potato Mode and dismisses it (matches warning wording); ESC in game opens pause/settings.
- Added global top-right Settings gear so the warning’s “right top” reference is always true.
- Added procedural ambience (wind, leaves, birds, footsteps) via Web Audio after user gesture.
- Added pause menu, settings drawer, live compass, zone names, timer/distance HUD.
- Potato Mode reduces grass/ferns, hides mist/flowers/mushrooms/leaf litter, disables shadows, lowers pixel ratio, increases fog.
- Time uses fixed 1/30s substeps so movement speed remains real-time on slow renderers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created full page/UI and responsive layouts, warning modal, start screen, HUD, pause/settings drawer, mobile joystick/jump button.
- Created procedural world: FBM terrain, winding trail ribbon, skydome shader, sun/fill/hemisphere lighting, fog, tree/grass/fern/stone/flower/mushroom/leaf-litter instancing, falling logs/stumps, mist, pollen, god rays, collision grid.
- Added player physics, spring arm/eye height, jump, head bob, footsteps, terrain collision, tree collision, world boundary.
- Added pointer-lock mouse look, touch-drag look, joystick analog movement, mobile jump.
- Added settings: Potato toggle, graphics select, FOV, sensitivity, volume, touch controls mode, reset to clearing.
- Added procedural audio.
- Desktop and mobile screenshots verified working; no JS page errors after favicon addition. Latest iteration improved lighting, sky, trail color, foliage detail, mobile title size, compass centering, hid mobile footer clutter, and added pointer-lock movement spike guard.
- Server running in tmux session `forest` at `http://localhost:3002/`.

### Active
- Validating the latest visual iteration via `/tmp/opencode/test-forest3.cjs` (written but not yet run) after changes to tree geometry textures, cinematic camera, mobile layout, and pointer-lock guard.

### Blocked
- None.

## Next Move
1. Run `DISPLAY=:0 node /tmp/opencode/test-forest3.cjs` and inspect new screenshots `22-start.png` through `27-mobile-play.png`.
2. Fix any remaining visual issues, especially pine/broadleaf appearance, start-screen cinematic framing, and mobile HUD/compass layout.
3. Test Potato Mode toggle from Settings and the warning’s “Turn On” path.
4. Test mobile joystick, jump button, and look-drag functionality with pointer events.
5. Test keyboard movement/jump and ESC warning behavior (`ESC` while warning open should enable Potato Mode).
6. Run final desktop/mobile capture and verify no console errors or 404s.
7. Commit changes if required by repository workflow.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: page structure, warning modal copy/buttons, start screen, HUD, settings, pause, mobile controls.
- `css/styles.css`: full visual system and responsive/mobile layout.
- `js/game.js`: controller, input, player physics, UI wiring, quality handling, pointer lock, animation loop.
- `js/world.js`: terrain generation, trail ribbon, sky shader, lighting, fog, collision grid, mist/motes/god rays, quality switching.
- `js/trees.js`: procedural pine/broadleaf/dead trees, logs, stumps, instancing, textures.
- `js/understory.js`: grass, ferns, shrubs, rocks, flowers, mushrooms, leaf litter, wind shader, Potato reduction.
- `js/textures.js`: procedural ground/path/bark/grass/needle/canopy/leaf/particle textures.
- `js/noise.js`: deterministic RNG/FBM/value noise/helpers.
- `js/audio.js`: procedural forest ambience.
- `vendor/three.module.min.js`: local Three.js r170 module.
- `/tmp/opencode/test-forest3.cjs`: latest Playwright screenshot test, not yet run.

import zlib, struct
def px(path,x,y):

    pos=8; idat=b''; w=h=0; ct=0; bd=0
    while pos<len(data):
        ln=struct.unpack('>I',data[pos:pos+4])[0]; typ=data[pos+4:pos+8]; chunk=data[pos+8:pos+8+ln]; pos+=12+ln
        if typ==b'IHDR':

        elif typ==b'IEND': break
    raw=zlib.decompress(idat); ch=4 if ct==6 else 3
    stride=w*ch; prev=bytearray(stride); out=[]
